claims.text: Au or AlN can serve as a high-thermal-conductivity passivation or encapsulation layer for the FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films.
Depositing the passivation layer will enhance heat extraction from the HEA films.
Depositing the passivation layer will stabilize surface or interface disorder.
Enhanced thermal extraction and stabilized interfaces will reduce heterogeneity among magnetostructural-transition nucleation sites.
The passivation layer will reduce thermal gradients during magnetic-cooling cycles.
The passivation layer will moderate nanoscale interfacial strain.
The passivation layer will moderate chemical inhomogeneity at nanoscale surfaces and interfaces.
Reduced interfacial heterogeneity will produce more homogeneous nucleation and growth of the magnetostructural transition.
Interface stabilization will lead to more uniform magnetostructural switching.
More uniform magnetostructural switching will narrow the thermal hysteresis.
More uniform magnetostructural switching will increase the magnetocaloric response.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, passivated films will have a reduced hysteresis width during low-field cycling.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, passivated films will have an enhanced peak magnetic entropy change during low-field cycling.
Peak magnetic entropy change is a measure of magnetocaloric performance.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films have pronounced surface or interface inhomogeneity and limited heat dissipation.
Surface or interface inhomogeneity and limited heat dissipation cause broader hysteresis and diminished magnetocaloric performance in the baseline films.
Heat-transfer inefficiencies and surface or interface effects dominate the response near the critical temperature at fields of a few hundred Oe to low kOe and at moderate cycling frequencies.
Heat-transfer capability limits the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
